reports.title: SLA report
reports.subtitle: Monthly evidence for each client contract. Attach it to your service report and invoice.
reports.target: Contract target: {{target}}% of tickets within SLA

footnote.tick: The dark mark on each bar is the {{target}}% target.

waiting.all: Time spent waiting on the client is excluded from SLA.
waiting.some: Time spent waiting on the client is excluded from SLA on the projects that pause the clock for it.
waiting.none: The SLA clock keeps running while a ticket waits on the client.

footnote.firstResponse: Average first response covers tickets reported in the portal; tickets the team logs are answered when logged.

empty.title: No clients yet
empty.body: Clients appear here once they are added in Settings › Clients.

mcp.title: MCP access
mcp.intro: Connect an AI assistant such as Claude Code or Cursor to SimDesk through MCP. It reads tickets in {{org}} and, with a read-and-write token, replies, adds internal notes and changes status, assignee and priority, all as you.
mcp.tokensIntro: A token works in {{org}} only, until it expires or you revoke it. Make one per device or client, so you can revoke one without the others.
mcp.empty: No tokens yet. Make one, then add SimDesk to your AI client with the settings below.

read.long: Finds and reads tickets, their conversation, activity and attachments.

write.long: Also replies to clients, adds internal notes and changes status, assignee and priority, as you.

mcp.revokeBody: Clients using this token stop working at their next request. You can make a new one any time.
mcp.connectIntro: Add SimDesk as a remote MCP server (HTTP) and send your token in the Authorization header. Replace the placeholder with your token.
mcp.claudeCodeHint: Run it in a terminal; Claude Code then lists SimDesk under /mcp.
mcp.otherClientsHint: For clients that read an mcpServers file with a url and headers, such as Cursor.
mcp.actsAsYou: Replies and notes the assistant writes appear under your name, and the client gets replies by email, as if you had sent them.
mcp.nameHint: Where you will use it, for example “Claude Code on my laptop”.
mcp.secretOnce: Shown only now. Copy it before you close this; if you lose it, revoke it and make another.
